1	Benchmark contamination is widely assumed to inflate language model scores, yet the actual effect has never been systematically measured across model families. We perform controlled SFT injection at five dosage levels into six models spanning five independent families (7B--14.7B parameters) and discover that contamination produces not one effect but qualitatively different dose-response patterns---from immunity (mean $\Delta < 1$\,percentage point [pp] across three seeds) through monotonic benefit ($+$2.4pp mean) to catastrophic collapse ($-$9 to $-$25pp across seeds). In our six-family sample, contamination vulnerability concentrates in the 65--70\% MMLU baseline band; models at extreme baselines show limited sensitivity. Counter-intuitively, the 14B Qwen model is 3$\times$ more fragile than 7B. These effects are benchmark-conditional: models harmed on MMLU can simultaneously benefit on GSM8K ($+$11pp), revealing asymmetric cross-benchmark transfer. Difference-in-differences analysis finds no item-specific memorization on MMLU (minimum detectable effect size 1.2--2.0pp); ARC has limited power (2.3--5.6pp).
